channel.title: Hartford Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hartford Business Journal (hartfordbusiness.com)

item.title: 🔒 Adopted in 2022 to ease student loan burdens and support workforce recruitment, CT tax credit program sees no takers
item.description: A Connecticut tax credit designed to help employers pay down workers' student loans has gone completely unused since its 2022 launch — and experts say poor promotion, administrative complexity and eligibility restrictions are largely to blame.

item.title: 🔒 CT biotech LambdaVision reserves spot on commercial space station to scale artificial retina
item.description: A Woodbridge-based biotech company has reserved space on the next commercial space station as it works to scale manufacturing of an artificial retina designed to restore vision in patients afflicted with degenerative eye diseases.

item.title: CT legislators consider bill to regulate ad volume on streaming services
item.description: A bill introduced in the General Law Committee and proposed by Sen. Bob Duff (D-Norwalk) would prohibit any streaming video service from transmitting commercials at a volume “that is louder than the volume established by the Federal Communications Commission” (FCC) for TV broadcast stations or cable TV providers.

item.title: $8M bonding bill would provide infrastructure support for tourism in Mystic
item.description: The funding could be used for docks, parking garages, establishing a shuttle boat service and establishing or improving riverwalks.

item.title: Luxury Home Sales: Waterfront home in East Lyme sells for $2.1M
item.description: Here’s a listing of recent luxury home sales in New Haven and New London counties. The data is provided by Evan Berman of the William Raveis Broder Team.

item.title: 🔒 Newington medical office property sells for $1.15M
item.description: A 4,500-square-foot medical office condominium in Newington has sold for $1.15 million.

item.title: Landlords, renters square off over eviction and rent bills
item.description: The state legislature’s Housing Committee is holding a public hearing Tuesday on 12 proposed bills, including five bills that seek to support renters.

item.title: SCSU expands AI in manufacturing training with new quantum, micro-credential program
item.description: Southern Connecticut State University said it is expanding its workforce training programs to address growing demand for artificial intelligence skills in Connecticut’s manufacturing sector.

item.title: 🔒 Lamont agenda targets taxes, AI rules, solar permits and warehouse quotas
item.description: Gov. Ned Lamont's 2026 legislative agenda touches on artificial intelligence guardrails, solar permitting, warehouse worker protections and tax relief for businesses — here's what Connecticut companies and nonprofits need to know.

item.title: 🔒 CT comptroller backs payment freezes for contractors in CT wage theft probes
item.description: State Comptroller Sean Scanlon urged state lawmakers on Tuesday to approve legislation that would allow his office to halt payments to contractors accused of violating Connecticut’s prevailing wage laws.
